title: Dodge D-Series Engines by Year (1961–1993)
description: Every factory engine in the Dodge D100, D150, W100 and W150 pickup by year, 1961–1993: slant sixes, LA and B V8s, the Li'l Red Express 360 and Magnums.
intro: Dodge's D-series pickups ran from 1961 to 1993; D means two-wheel drive and W four-wheel drive, sold as the Power Wagon. This page covers the half-tons: the D100 and W100, renamed D150 and W150 from 1978. The 1994 Ram 1500 replaced them.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first D-series used the 170 and 225 slant sixes and the 318 V8, with the 383 from 1967. In 1964–1966 Dodge offered a high-performance package with the 413 and then the 426 wedge.
The 1972 redesign offered the 225 six and the 318, 360, 400 and 440 V8s. The 1978–1979 Li'l Red Express used a 225 hp 360, and a Mitsubishi diesel was listed for 1978. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.
The restyled trucks used the 225 six and the 318 and 360 V8s, then the 3.9 V6 from 1988 and fuel-injected Magnum engines from 1992.
